MEASURED, not inferred: hosting a webhook receiver turned this storyboard from wholly skipped into 8 graded failures (capability_discovery, fetch_brand_json, trigger_webhook_operation, trigger_operation_id_echo, trigger_idempotent_webhook_initial, trigger_retry_scenario, trigger_signed_webhook, assert_webhook_signing_key_present). The three webhook issues that were mapped here first cover NONE of them: #1639 is lifecycle emission — WHEN a terminal webhook is enqueued — and says so ("lifecycle-final largely ungraded in conformance"); #1735 and #1712 are test-infra, grading our own UC-004 BDD scenarios on a real receiver rather than production behaviour, and #1735 targets the DEPRECATED HMAC fallback rather than RFC 9421. The 3 signing-side checks (fetch_brand_json, trigger_signed_webhook, assert_webhook_signing_key_present) ARE addressed by #1291, whose implementation branch signs webhook deliveries under the webhook profile tag ("adcp/webhook-signing/v1") and publishes JWKS at /.well-known/jwks.json governed by brand.json's jwks_uri. Judge #1291 by that branch, not by its TL;DR: the issue text argues REQUEST signing is optional and capability-advertised, which is true and is a different thing — webhook signing is a separate profile and baseline in 3.0 unless the buyer opts into the deprecated HMAC fallback. Genuinely untracked are the payload-correlation and idempotency requirements: operation_id echoed from push_notification_config (sellers MUST NOT derive it by parsing the receiver URL), idempotency_key present and byte-stable across retries (adcp#2417), and replay of an idempotent request not emitting a second logical webhook. Those are #1869.
